primitives.name: Branch Divergence Index
primitives.verbatim_quote: `motif/research-push-all` — 36 ahead, 0 behind Commits (all 2026-10-02, "two-host transfer from Motif VM"): ~15× `Research: arxiv-sweep...` + ~21× `Research: corpus-intelligence...`.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'D_{\\text{div}}': 'dimensionless divergence index', 'C_{\\text{ahead}}': 'integer number of ahead commits', 'C_{\\text{behind}}': 'integer number of behind commits'}
primitives.assumptions: Commits are timestamped and linearly ordered; divergence is computed relative to main branch.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When $ C_{\text{ahead}} > 0 $, indicates active development; when $ C_{\text{behind}} > 0 $, indicates stale merge.

layer2.mapping: The divergence index mirrors the Bayesian posterior update of branch consistency against mainline, where $ D_{\text{div}} = \log \frac{P(\text{branch} | \text{main})}{P(\text{branch} | \neg \text{main})} $.
layer2.telemetry: Number of ahead/behind commits in git diff API.

primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'H_{\\text{tree}}': 'homology class of file tree', 'N_{\\text{files}}': 'integer number of files in tree', 'T_{\\text{paths}}': 'recursive path count'}

It acts as a proxy for information entropy in the codebase's development flow. File tree homology $ H_{\text{tree}} $ quantifies structural changes in the repository, using recursive path enumeration to detect novel directories or file additions. The artifact snapshot manifest $ M_{\text{snap}} $ provides a deterministic view of pipeline state at a given moment, enabling version control and reproducibility checks. These three primitives form a triadic system: divergence drives change, homology tracks structure, and manifests anchor state. Failure modes include API truncation (missing files), divergent commits (merge conflicts), and inconsistent snapshots (data loss).
